laws.act: Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882
laws.summary: Mandates that a month-to-month lease termination notice must be in writing and serve a minimum of 15 days in advance. Failure to give a full 15-day notice can dismiss the eviction in court.
remedies: Verify if notice is served 15 days prior to lease termination date.
Check if notice is signed by the landlord or authorized representative.
Collect bank statements or payment receipts proving timely rent payments.

laws.act: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
laws.summary: Deals with the criminal offense of cheque dishonor due to insufficient funds. The payee must send a written demand notice within 30 days of bounce, and the drawer gets 15 days to pay before a complaint can be filed.
remedies: Verify if the bounce notice was sent within 30 days of the dishonor memo.
Settle the cheque amount within 15 days of receiving the notice to avoid criminal liability.
Draft a formal reply stating transaction proof or disputing liability.

laws.summary: Mandates that an electricity distribution company must serve a written notice of at least 15 clear days before disconnecting supply. Consumers can dispute the dues in court or consumer forums.
remedies: Check if 15 clear days notice was given in writing before power cut.
Verify electricity bill calculation errors or payment receipts.
File an appeal with the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF).

laws.act: Section 19 of the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
laws.summary: Governs applications filed by banks or financial institutions in the Debts Recovery Tribunal (DRT) to recover outstanding dues from default borrowers.
remedies: Verify the statement of account and calculation of interest rates.
File a written reply statement disputing calculations or terms within 30 days.
Approach the bank for a One-Time Settlement (OTS) option.

laws.act: Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) / BNS Equivalent
laws.summary: Deals with criminal defamation where a person makes false spoken or written imputations intending to harm a citizen's reputation.
remedies: Check if the statement made is true and for public good (truth is a defense).
Reply denying malicious intent or proving the statements represent fair comment.
Draft legal response requesting withdrawal of demand notice.
